attrs.evidence: The schema is GPT-5.6's decomposition, adopted here as the replacement for TAX-AUTH's single enum. Cell 24 is the worked instance and it is honest in the new schema and inexpressible in the old: enforcement_mode `precondition` (the gate `(1-eta)^n <= delta` is a total predicate over the certificate), guarantee_mode `probabilistic` (domination is certified at confidence 1-delta, never established), failure_semantics `refuse` (below budget, no escalation). What is NOT conceded is the direction Fable defended: the separations BETWEEN enforcement classes are theorems, not conventions — an execution monitor cannot enforce a non-safety property (Schneider), and edit automata characterise a strictly larger class (Ligatti et al.) — so a checker may refuse an incoherent combination. But importing a refusal theorem requires the monitor model to be declared first, and this record does not declare one.
attrs.gap: The 46 cells are NOT retyped into the three fields. Only cell 24 is worked as an example, and the table still renders one authority string per cell. Retyping is Phase 2.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 (Mosaic audit, 2026-08-24) for the three-field decomposition. Schneider 2000 (Enforceable Security Policies); Ligatti, Bauer, Walker (edit automata) for the class separations, cited for what they prove and not for a kind -> enforcement mapping.
attrs.statement: An authority entry is three fields, not one: (enforcement_mode: precondition | postcondition | monitor | advisory) x (guarantee_mode: deterministic | probabilistic | conditional) x (failure_semantics: refuse | quarantine | compensate | none). A statistical or environmental evidence basis MAY feed a deterministic precondition gate; the guarantee stays probabilistic unless a separate deterministic proof discharges the underlying proposition.
